# 7414 - Hex Schmitt-trigger inverter

Package DIP-14 · family 74 · catalogue file [catalog/chips/7414.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/7414.json)

## Symbol

| As printed in ND-13.003.01, page 7 | Drawn in ND style | Drawn in modern style |
|---|---|---|
| ![7414 as printed in the 1976 symbol manual](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/7414.png) | ![7414 drawn in nd style](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/shapes/not-schmitt1.png) | ![7414 drawn in modern style](../../../catalog/symbols/modern/shapes/not-schmitt1.png) |

The inverter rectangle (triangle inside) with its top edge running on to the right and its bottom edge running on to the left. What a Schmitt trigger is: a normal TTL input switches at one voltage, so a slow or noisy signal near that voltage makes the output flicker between 0 and 1 several times. A Schmitt trigger input has two switching points instead: the input must rise above about 1.7 V before the output changes, and then fall below about 0.9 V before it changes back. The gap between them (the hysteresis) means noise and slow edges give one clean change. It is used on signals from cables, switches and RC delay circuits. The input still reads as plain logic 0 or 1; only its noise tolerance differs.

How to tell it on a drawing: Inverter + extended edges = Schmitt inverter.

All symbols: [symbol catalogue](../../SYMBOL-CATALOG.md).

## Propagation delays

All measured at VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, RL 400 ohm, CL 15 pF.

| From | To | Edge | Typ ns | Max ns |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| any | Y | PLH | 15 | 22 |
| any | Y | PHL | 15 | 22 |

## Notes

The datasheet gives no minimum propagation delay; minNs is null (the path-delay function uses 0 ns). No setup/hold/pulse-width limits apply to a gate, so timingLimits is empty.
